title: The Escape from Politics: Frankfurt, the Seeing Stone, and the House in Barrio Parque
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, born in the Federal Republic
stops.date_confidence: attested to 11 October 1967 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'). No source names the birth hospital; an earlier research pass proposed the Universitaetsklinikum Frankfurt coordinate, which is both unsupported and off by some hundreds of metres, so the city point is used instead.
stops.campa: Peter Andreas Thiel is born in Frankfurt am Main on the eleventh of October, to Klaus Thiel, an engineer, and his wife Susanne. The city is twenty-two years out of its own rubble. No source names the hospital, and no biographer has found a reason to look for it; the birth is a line on a document, the first of a great many documents. Within the year the family will be gone. He keeps the German citizenship and the German language. The country itself he will not remember.
suggested_refs: Frankfurt am Main civil registry, October 1967

stops.name: Cleveland, the first American address
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1968 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); month and day are not recorded and default to January. No source names the suburb or the street, so the coordinate is downtown Cleveland as the nearest fixed landmark.
stops.campa: Klaus Thiel's engineering work brings the family across the Atlantic before the boy's second birthday, and the first American address is somewhere in the Cleveland area. Nobody wrote down which street. The city is at the top of its industrial arc and starting the long fall, and the Thiels are not there to see either; within a few years they are gone again. Peter will pass through seven schools before he is ten. Forty-eight years later he will walk onto a stage in this same city and endorse a candidate for president of the United States.
suggested_refs: Klaus Thiel's employment record as a chemical and mining engineer, not located in any reachable source

stops.name: Swakopmund, the German school on the Namib coast
stops.date_confidence: attested to a window of roughly 1971-1977 for the family's South African and South West African years (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the date is the start of that window and month and day are defaulted. The two years at the Swakopmund school are attested; their exact placement inside the window is not.
stops.campa: The family moves to southern Africa, and for about two years the boy attends a German-language school in Swakopmund, a colonial seaside town on the Namib coast held by South Africa under a mandate it has stopped pretending is temporary. The German community of the town is known in this decade for a continued glorification of Nazism. He is a small boy in a school uniform in a country where the law sorts people by colour, and he is on the side the law favours. Lessons are in German. Discipline includes beating.
suggested_refs: The Deutsche Hoehere Privatschule and the German-language schools of Swakopmund under South African administration

stops.name: Arandis, the mine on the gravel plain
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and a contradiction left standing. The dossier ties Klaus Thiel's work to the Roessing uranium mine, seventy kilometres inland from Swakopmund; no independent source confirms the employer. Wikipedia, 'Roessing uranium mine', gives the start of operations as 1976, which cannot underwrite a father's uranium job across the early 1970s. The coordinate is corrected to the mine's own position, 22 degrees 29 minutes S, 15 degrees 02 minutes E. The claim that the ore fed South Africa's clandestine nuclear programme has no citation in any source reached and is not carried here.
stops.campa: On the gravel plain inland from the coast, the largest open-pit uranium mine in the world is cut into the Namib. Roessing begins production in 1976 with Iranian money in its share register and a workforce housed by race. The record that puts Klaus Thiel here is a single unsourced assertion, and the dates do not sit still: the family's African years open in 1971, the pit opens in 1976, and the two windows barely touch. What is certain is that the father was a mining engineer and that the son grew up close to the extraction business. The rest is claim.
suggested_refs: Roessing Uranium Limited shareholding and labour records, 1970s

stops.name: Foster City, the house without a television
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1977 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); month and day are not recorded and are defaulted. The chess-set sticker reading Born to Win is a dossier detail, uncorroborated.
stops.campa: The wandering stops on landfill in San Mateo County, in a planned suburb built on mud pumped out of the bay twenty years earlier. He enters fifth grade at Bowditch Middle School and finishes first in a California-wide mathematics competition. There is no television in the house until junior high. He plays chess seriously enough to rank nationally among juniors and eventually to hold the Life Master title of the United States Chess Federation, and a sticker on his chess set is said to read Born to Win.
suggested_refs: United States Chess Federation Life Master records
sources: dossier, for the household and chess detail

stops.name: San Mateo High School, first in his class
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1985 (Wikipedia, 'San Mateo High School'); the graduation month and day are not recorded and June is a default. The coordinate is corrected to the campus at 506 North Delaware Street; an earlier pass placed it 2.7 km south.
stops.campa: He graduates valedictorian of the public high school on North Delaware Street. The reading of his adolescence is Tolkien, read and reread, then Ayn Rand, then Solzhenitsyn: three writers who agree that the world is being run badly by people who cannot see what is in front of them. The chess has taught him a thing the classroom has not, which is how to sit across from one other person and want them to lose. He is seventeen. Stanford is four miles down the peninsula.
suggested_refs: San Mateo High School yearbook, class of 1985

segments.name: Stanford: The Review, Girard, the Law

stops.name: Stanford University, philosophy and mimetic desire
stops.date_confidence: the 1985-1989 undergraduate years and the 1989 B.A. in philosophy are attested (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the September date orders the segment and is not a recorded arrival.
stops.campa: He reads philosophy. In the humanities quad he encounters Rene Girard, then teaching at Stanford, and the theory that human desire is not original but copied: that we want what other people want, that we come to resemble whoever we compete with, and that a crowd resolves its accumulated rivalry by agreeing on one victim it can destroy together. Thiel takes this not as an interpretation of literature but as a description of how the world actually runs. He will spend the next forty years applying it to markets and to himself.
suggested_refs: Rene Girard, Deceit, Desire and the Novel; Violence and the Sacred; Things Hidden Since the Foundation of the World

stops.name: Stanford campus, the first issue of the Review
stops.date_confidence: attested: first issue dated 9 June 1987, founded by Thiel with Norman Book, Thiel editor in chief 1987-1989 (Wikipedia, 'The Stanford Review'). An earlier pass gave the founding context as Stanford's speech code; that is an anachronism, the code was not adopted until 1990. The attested trigger is the Rainbow Coalition march and the Rainbow Agenda.
stops.campa: Some five hundred students march behind Jesse Jackson across the campus and present a document called the Rainbow Agenda. Thiel founds a newspaper with Norman Book to supply what its own masthead calls an alternative viewpoint, and edits it for two years from the age of nineteen. The paper is small and its circulation is a campus. What it actually builds is a roster: the writers and editors who pass through it turn up later at PayPal, at Palantir, at Thiel Capital and in Republican administrations.
suggested_refs: The Stanford Review, first issue, 9 June 1987

stops.name: Stanford Law School, the J.D. and The Diversity Myth
stops.date_confidence: the 1992 J.D. is attested (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); month and day are not recorded and June is a default. The Supreme Court clerkship rejection is a dossier claim, not independently corroborated in this pass, and is carried as reconstruction.
stops.campa: He stays on the same campus for law school and takes the degree in 1992. With David Sacks, another Review alumnus, he works up the arguments about multiculturalism and campus speech that will be published in 1995 as The Diversity Myth. He applies for a clerkship at the Supreme Court of the United States and does not get it. By his own later account the rejection knocked the rungs out of a ladder he had been climbing for fifteen years without once asking where it went.
suggested_refs: Peter Thiel and David Sacks, The Diversity Myth (Independent Institute, 1995)

stops.name: Atlanta, the Eleventh Circuit clerkship
stops.date_confidence: the clerkship for Judge James Larry Edmondson of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit is attested (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the term's start month is not recorded and September is a default. The coordinate is the Eleventh Circuit's Atlanta courthouse, not confirmed chambers.
stops.campa: For a year he clerks for Judge James Larry Edmondson of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, reading trial records and drafting opinions in a federal courthouse in downtown Atlanta. It is the most conventional year of his life and the last one. The appellate bench is the terminal station of the credential he has been accumulating since Bowditch Middle School, and having arrived there he finds he has no further interest in the line. He does not stay in Atlanta.
suggested_refs: Chambers of Judge James Larry Edmondson, Eleventh Circuit, 1992-1993

stops.name: 125 Broad Street, New York: under a year at Sullivan and Cromwell
stops.date_confidence: attested that the tenure ran under one year (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the widely repeated seven-months figure is not in that source and is not used. Month and day are defaulted. Coordinate corrected to the firm's 125 Broad Street address. The Credit Suisse currency-options desk and the speechwriting for William Bennett are attested but their New York locations are not, so they are recorded inside this stop rather than given pins of their own.
stops.campa: He takes the securities job at Sullivan and Cromwell in lower Manhattan and is out of the building inside a year. He moves to a currency options desk at Credit Suisse and writes speeches on the side for William Bennett, the former education secretary, which is the first time he is paid for political language rather than legal language. Then he goes back to California, three years older and no warmer about the city. Of the law firm he says afterwards that everyone outside it wanted to get in and everyone inside it wanted to get out.
suggested_refs: Sullivan and Cromwell LLP, 125 Broad Street, New York

segments.name: Confinity, PayPal, and the Palace Coup

stops.name: Palo Alto, Thiel Capital and the founding of Confinity
stops.date_confidence: attested to December 1998 for the founding with Max Levchin and Luke Nosek and the initial roughly $100,000 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); day defaulted. The 1996 founding of Thiel Capital Management on roughly $1 million is separately attested. Palo Alto is the company's widely reported base; no 1998 street address was confirmed.
stops.campa: Back in California he has been running a small fund called Thiel Capital Management on roughly a million dollars raised from family and friends. In December he puts a hundred thousand of it into a company founded with Max Levchin and Luke Nosek, called Fieldlink and then Confinity, whose product is a way to beam encrypted money between PalmPilot handhelds. Almost nobody wants to beam money between PalmPilots. The version that works over email, built as an afterthought, is the one that takes, and it is called PayPal.
suggested_refs: Confinity incorporation records, December 1998

stops.name: Palo Alto, the referral bonus and the burn
stops.date_confidence: the 1999 launch of the PayPal service is attested (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the October date orders the segment and is not a recorded event date. The fraud, burn rate and X.com merger are attested in the biography and the dossier without precise dating.
stops.campa: The service grows by paying people to sign up and paying them again to bring a friend, ten dollars at a time, and it grows fastest inside eBay auctions, where strangers have to pay strangers. It also bleeds. Fraud rings work it from Eastern Europe and the burn rate eats capital by the month. In March 2000 it merges with a rival across the street called X.com, run by a South African of the same age with the same certainty about everything. The merged company has one market and two chief executives, each of whom believes the other is wrong about how to run it.
suggested_refs: The X.com and Confinity merger agreement, March 2000

stops.name: Palo Alto, removed while away
stops.date_confidence: attested. The September 2000 board removal of Musk while he was abroad on honeymoon, and Thiel's installation as chief executive, are recorded in elon_musk.journey.json and independently corroborated by the dossier. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from that file's Palo Alto stop. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: In September the board of the merged company moves against Elon Musk while he is out of the country on his honeymoon, and installs Thiel as chief executive. Musk will call it a palace coup for the rest of his life. Thiel does not dispute the description so much as the premise that a coup is a bad outcome when the alternative is a company dying of split command. He cancels the rebuild onto Microsoft software, keeps the PayPal brand over the X.com one, and in June of the following year the merged firm formally takes that name.
suggested_refs: elon_musk.journey.json, stop 'Palo Alto, removed while away', 2000-09-01

stops.name: Nasdaq, New York: thirteen dollars a share
stops.date_confidence: attested to 15 February 2002 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'). Trading is electronic; the coordinate is the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, the conventional physical landmark for such listings, and no source places Thiel there in person.
stops.campa: PayPal goes public at thirteen dollars a share and raises more than sixty million, one of the very few technology listings to get out alive in the two years after the crash. The market it walks into has spent that time punishing exactly this kind of company. He has proved, in the only arithmetic that ends arguments, that the thing he built is worth money, and he has proved it in front of everyone who mattered to him at Stanford. Thiel is thirty-four.
suggested_refs: PayPal Inc. Form S-1 and the February 2002 offering prospectus

stops.name: eBay headquarters, San Jose: the sale closes
stops.date_confidence: attested, with a contradiction left standing. Wikipedia's 'Peter Thiel' gives $1.5 billion; Wikipedia's 'eBay' gives completion on 3 October 2002 at $1.4 billion. The first is the July announced all-stock value, the second the closing value; both are recorded rather than reconciled. Thiel's roughly 3.7 percent stake and roughly $55 million in proceeds are attested. Coordinate corrected to eBay's Willow Glen headquarters, six kilometres from the downtown point used in an earlier pass.
stops.campa: Eight months after the listing, eBay buys the company that had been feeding on its own auctions. The all-stock value announced in July was one and a half billion dollars; the value at closing on the third of October was one point four. Thiel holds about three point seven percent and leaves with something near fifty-five million. The engineers and executives scatter and over the following decade found or fund Tesla, SpaceX, YouTube, LinkedIn, Yelp and Palantir. The press begins calling them the PayPal Mafia, which is not a name any of them chose.
suggested_refs: eBay Inc. announcement of the PayPal acquisition, July 2002, and its October 2002 completion

segments.name: The Fund, the Seeing Stone, the Network

stops.name: San Francisco, Clarium Capital
stops.date_confidence: contradiction not resolved. Wikipedia's 'Clarium Capital' gives a 2002 founding in San Francisco; Wikipedia's 'Peter Thiel' gives 2003. Month and day are unrecorded and defaulted, which places this stop before the October 2002 sale that supplied the capital, an ordering problem inherent to the contradiction. Peak assets of about $8 billion in 2008 and the fall to about $350 million by 2011 are attested on the Clarium page.
stops.campa: He puts ten million dollars of the PayPal money into a global macro hedge fund and bets on the largest things he can find: currencies, the price of oil, the end of cheap energy, the proposition that the developed world stopped growing decades ago and has not yet admitted it. For five years the bets work and the fund swells past eight billion under management. Then they stop working, and the money leaves considerably faster than it came in. By 2011 the fund holds around three hundred and fifty million dollars.
suggested_refs: Clarium Capital Management LLC, SEC filings 2003-2011

stops.name: Palo Alto, Palantir incorporated
stops.date_confidence: attested to 6 May 2003, with the five named co-founders, roughly $30 million in initial funding largely from Thiel, and In-Q-Tel's roughly $2 million (Wikipedia, 'Palantir Technologies'). An earlier pass hedged the date as 2003/2004 and treated the funding figures as dossier-only; both cautions were unnecessary. The internal name of the Palo Alto headquarters, the Shire, is attested on the same page.
stops.campa: Incorporated on the sixth of May with Alex Karp, Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale and Nathan Gettings, to sell the fraud-detection logic PayPal built against Russian card rings to intelligence agencies instead of to merchants. Thiel supplies most of the thirty million in initial funding. The CIA venture arm In-Q-Tel adds about two million and, more usefully, adds customers. He names it for the palantiri of Tolkien, the seeing stones that show a watcher anything at any distance and can be turned by a stronger hand to show only what it wants shown. The Palo Alto office is called the Shire.
suggested_refs: In-Q-Tel investment in Palantir Technologies, 2005

stops.name: Stanford, the Girard seminar and the apocalypse paper
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier reports a small Stanford seminar convened by Thiel with the chaplain Robert Hamerton-Kelly, bringing together Rene Girard and the Girardian scholar Wolfgang Palaver; no independent source was reached. The 'Politics and Apocalypse' paper is attested only through a secondary summary of Joshua Tait's work, and the conference venue and date were not confirmed, so it is recorded at Thiel's own Stanford pin rather than given a pin it cannot support. Month and day defaulted. The collection of the same name was published in 2007.
stops.campa: He comes back to the campus as a patron rather than a student. With the Stanford chaplain Robert Hamerton-Kelly he convenes a small seminar around Girard and the Girardian scholar Wolfgang Palaver. In the same period he gives the circle a paper arguing that the West after the eleventh of September has been left defenceless by its own commitments to democracy and equality, that the scapegoat mechanism Girard described was never abolished by liberalism but only concealed, and that something will have to restrain what is coming. It is published in 2007 in a collection called Politics and Apocalypse.
stops.quote: The reign of science foretold in New Atlantis culminated and terminated at Los Alamos.
stops.quote_source: Peter Thiel, 'Against Edenism', First Things, June/July 2015, eleven years after this seminar and stating its conclusion
suggested_refs: Robert Hamerton-Kelly, ed., Politics and Apocalypse (Michigan State University Press, 2007)
sources: Joshua Tait, cited via Wikipedia, 'Neoreactionary movement'

stops.name: Palo Alto, the five hundred thousand dollars
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 2004, $500,000 for 10.2 percent at a valuation near $4.9 million (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); day defaulted. The coordinate marks Facebook's earliest Palo Alto office, the landmark for the company at the time; the negotiation itself may have taken place elsewhere.
stops.campa: Reid Hoffman brings him a Harvard sophomore with a website for college students. Thiel writes a cheque for five hundred thousand dollars against a valuation under five million, and takes ten point two percent and a seat on the board. He says later that what let him understand the thing on sight was Girard: a machine for showing millions of people, continuously and free of charge, exactly what other people want. The investment returns roughly a thousandfold over the following eight years.
suggested_refs: Thefacebook Inc. Series A documentation, August 2004

stops.name: The Presidio, San Francisco: Founders Fund
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 2005, founded by Thiel, Ken Howery and Luke Nosek (Wikipedia, 'Founders Fund'); day defaulted. Correcting an earlier pass: Sean Parker was not a founder, he joined in 2006 and stayed until 2014. Coordinate is the fund's Letterman Digital Arts Center headquarters in the Presidio rather than a generic city point.
stops.campa: With Howery and Nosek he sets up a venture firm in an old army post at the mouth of the Golden Gate, in the building George Lucas raised on the site of the military hospital. The thesis is stated mostly in the negative: do not diversify, do not remove the founder, do not fund a company that has competitors. Look for the one nobody else is doing, and hold it. Sean Parker joins the following year. SpaceX, Palantir, Airbnb, Stripe and Anduril follow in their turn.
stops.quote: We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters.
stops.quote_source: Founders Fund manifesto, 'What Happened to the Future?', 2011, quoted in The New Yorker, 21 November 2011. Frequently misattributed to a Yale commencement address, which Thiel never gave
suggested_refs: Founders Fund, 'The Founders Fund Manifesto: What Happened to the Future?' (2011)

stops.name: New York, Gawker prints the headline
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2007 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'); the exact publication date is not carried in the source used and month and day are defaulted. Coordinate is Manhattan; Gawker Media's office address is not confirmed in the sources reached.
stops.campa: A blog with a small staff and a large readership runs a piece under the headline Peter Thiel is totally gay, people. He is forty. He has told his family and not his industry, and the piece takes the choice away from him in an afternoon, in front of everyone he does business with. There is no lawsuit, no statement, no visible response of any kind for nine years; he goes on funding companies and writing about liberty and about the sea. In an office in New York the writers move to the next post before the end of the day. The piece stays online.
suggested_refs: Gawker, 'Peter Thiel is totally gay, people' (2007)

stops.name: San Francisco, the seed money for seasteading
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2008 for the initial $500,000 donation to the Seasteading Institute, with the last Thiel donation in 2014 (dossier, corroborating widely reported figures); month and day defaulted. Coordinate is the institute's San Francisco base, not a confirmed street address.
stops.campa: He gives five hundred thousand dollars to the Seasteading Institute, founded by Patri Friedman and Wayne Gramlich to build sovereign floating communities in international water. The premise is that no existing state can be reformed from inside it, and that on a fully claimed planet the only unclaimed ground left is the sea, where a political order could be started from nothing and then left alone. He keeps funding it until 2014, by which point the milestones have not been met and the donations stop. No platform is ever built.
stops.quote: I have focused my efforts on new technologies that may create a new space for freedom.
stops.quote_source: Peter Thiel, 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound, 13 April 2009
suggested_refs: The Seasteading Institute, founding prospectus and annual reports 2008-2014

stops.name: San Francisco, The Education of a Libertarian
stops.date_confidence: attested to 13 April 2009, the essay's publication date in Cato Unbound; quotations verified against the essay text. The essay has no place. The coordinate is Thiel's own San Francisco base at the time and marks the writer, not the writing. Nick Land's coinage of the Dark Enlightenment was serialised on his own blog from late 2012; Wikipedia gives no year for the essay itself, dating only the 2022 Imperium Press book edition, so the three-year interval stated here rests on the serialisation date and is soft.
stops.campa: He publishes an essay in a Cato Institute journal that will be quoted against him for the rest of his life. It says he no longer believes freedom and democracy are compatible; that the extension of the franchise to women and the growth of welfare have made capitalist democracy an oxymoron; that the great task for libertarians is to find an escape from politics in all its forms. He names three escapes, and they are cyberspace, outer space, and the sea. Some years later Nick Land, working Curtis Yarvin's blog up into what he calls the Dark Enlightenment, cites this essay among the movement's sources.
stops.quote: Most importantly, I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.
stops.quote_source: Peter Thiel, 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound, 13 April 2009
suggested_refs: Peter Thiel, 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound, 13 April 2009
nick_land.journey.json, for the Dark Enlightenment material
sources: Peter Thiel, 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound, 13 April 2009

stops.name: San Francisco, the anti-Rhodes scholarship
stops.date_confidence: attested: announced at TechCrunch Disrupt in September 2010 and established in 2011, conceived by Thiel as an anti-Rhodes scholarship, stipend $100,000 over two years and raised to $250,000 beginning with the 2026 class (Wikipedia, 'Thiel Fellowship'). Day defaulted. Coordinate is the Thiel Foundation's San Francisco base, which moves to Los Angeles in 2018.
stops.campa: At a conference in September he announces a fellowship that pays people under twenty to leave university and build something instead. He calls it an anti-Rhodes scholarship. The argument underneath it is that American higher education has become a positional good sold on fear, a tournament producing conformity and debt, and that the most capable young people are precisely the ones who lose most by entering it. Universities respond as though attacked. The stipend is a hundred thousand dollars across two years, raised to two hundred and fifty thousand for the class of 2026.
suggested_refs: Thiel Fellowship announcement, TechCrunch Disrupt, September 2010

stops.name: New Haven, the talk at Yale Law School
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 2011 Yale Law School talk and the meeting with J. D. Vance are the widely reported origin of the relationship and are carried in the dossier; no primary account of the talk was reached. Month and day defaulted. Vance joining Mithril Capital in 2016, the founding of Narya Capital, and the roughly $15 million backing of the 2022 Ohio Senate campaign are reported rather than independently verified here.
stops.campa: He speaks at the law school in New Haven, and a second-year student from Middletown, Ohio stays behind afterwards to say something to him once the applause is over. J. D. Vance will join Mithril Capital, the growth fund Thiel launches the following year, then found Narya Capital with Thiel's support, then take some fifteen million dollars from him for a Senate campaign in Ohio in 2022. None of that exists yet, and none of it is written down at the time.
suggested_refs: Mithril Capital Management, launched June 2012 with roughly $402 million in initial assets

stops.name: Christchurch, a million dollars into the rubble
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier reports that officials cited a NZ$1 million donation toward Christchurch earthquake relief in support of the citizenship grant; the New Zealand government release was not retrieved. Month and day are defaulted to January, which precedes the 22 February 2011 earthquake the donation answered; the default is a schema artefact, not a claim about sequence.
stops.campa: In February a shallow earthquake kills a hundred and eighty-five people in the second city of New Zealand and brings down its cathedral. Thiel gives a million New Zealand dollars toward the relief. By one accounting he has at this point spent twelve days in the country. When officials come to write the justification for the citizenship he applied for in January, the donation goes into the file alongside his entrepreneurship and his investments there. He has never lived in New Zealand.
suggested_refs: New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs file on the section 9(1)(c) citizenship grant, released 2017

stops.name: Santa Monica, the New Zealand passport
stops.date_confidence: the 2011 grant under a discretionary ministerial exception, and its disclosure by journalism in 2017, are attested (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'). The January application, the section 9(1)(c) clause, the private ceremony at the New Zealand consulate in Santa Monica on 30 June 2011 and the twelve days spent in the country come from the dossier's account of the released official file, which was not retrieved directly in this pass.
stops.campa: In a consulate office on the California coast he takes the oath and becomes a citizen of New Zealand under section nine, subsection one, paragraph c of the Citizenship Act, the clause reserved for grants in the public interest. A minister signs the exception. Nothing is announced. One of the most conspicuous men in Silicon Valley now holds a second nationality at the far end of the Pacific, and it stays out of public view until a reporter files the right request in 2017.
stops.quote: the great task for libertarians is to find an escape from politics in all its forms
stops.quote_source: Peter Thiel, 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound, 13 April 2009
suggested_refs: New Zealand Citizenship Act 1977, section 9(1)(c)

segments.name: The Classroom and the Cash Out

stops.name: Stanford, CS183
stops.date_confidence: attested: CS183, Startup, taught in the spring quarter of 2012, with Blake Masters's notes later revised with Thiel into Zero to One (Wikipedia, 'Zero to One'). The April date orders the segment; no session dates are recorded here.
stops.campa: He teaches an undergraduate course on startups, in the buildings where he learned the material himself, and a law student named Blake Masters takes notes and posts them online. The notes travel further and faster than anything Thiel has published under his own name. The argument is one sentence stretched across ten weeks: competition is for losers, every valuable company is a monopoly that has escaped comparison, and the interesting question about a business plan is not how you will beat the others but why there are no others.
stops.quote: Brilliant thinking is rare, but courage is in even shorter supply than genius.
stops.quote_source: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, Zero to One, Crown Business, 2014, out of the CS183 lectures
suggested_refs: Blake Masters's CS183 lecture notes, blakemasters.com, spring 2012

stops.name: Nasdaq, New York: the Facebook shares
stops.date_confidence: attested: 16.8 million shares sold for about $638 million at the May 2012 IPO, the remaining stake for about $395.8 million in August 2012 (Wikipedia, 'Peter Thiel'). Trading is electronic and the coordinate is the Nasdaq MarketSite, a landmark rather than a place Thiel occupied.
stops.campa: Facebook lists on the eighteenth of May and the offering goes badly, the stock breaking issue within days and the underwriters blamed for months. Thiel sells sixteen point eight million shares for about six hundred and thirty-eight million dollars, and in August sells most of what is left for another three hundred and ninety-five. The criticism for selling early into a company he helped build follows him for years, and the arithmetic on the original half million answers none of it. He keeps the board seat for another decade.
suggested_refs: Facebook Inc. Form 4 filings, May and August 2012

stops.name: New York, Zero to One
stops.date_confidence: attested: published 16 September 2014 by Crown Business, by Thiel with Blake Masters, out of the spring 2012 CS183 lectures (Wikipedia, 'Zero to One'). Coordinate corrected to the imprint's Penguin Random House address at 1745 Broadway; an earlier pass used a Grand Central point. Thiel was not necessarily present there. The interlanguage evidence shows at least eleven other-language editions, but individual publishers and dates were not confirmed.
stops.campa: The lecture notes become a book, written up with Masters and published by a Random House imprint on Broadway. It sells in the millions and appears in at least eleven other languages. What the essays never managed, the book does: it makes the argument portable. A founder in Bangalore or in Lagos who has never heard of Rene Girard now has the doctrine in two hundred pages, in the imperative mood, with a chapter on why the secrets are still there for anyone willing to look for them.

stops.campa: Gawker.com publishes its last post on the twenty-second of August, Nick Denton writing under the title How Things Work, and stops. The company had filed for bankruptcy in June; the other sites are sold to Univision and go on under a different name. A week earlier Thiel had argued in the New York Times that a publication which posts a private citizen's sex tape is not doing journalism, and that funding the suit was one of his greater philanthropic acts. A sex tape was published without the consent of the man in it; the company that published it is gone; the money that closed it belonged to a man it had named nine years earlier.
